propositions: Historical mutation score ceilings are stale; signing.py now generates 814 mutants versus old record of 491, including real contract gaps that cannot be bulk-fingerprinted.

Shard enforcement modes (advisory, ratchet, strict) are defined in a manifest and control whether mutation outcomes block CI: advisory runs head only and reports nonblocking findings; ratchet compares fresh base/head and blocks regressions for unchanged functions; strict requires all mutants killed or individually fingerprinted.
Shard selection maps changed source/test/support files and global inputs to shards via a deterministic selector that reports unmatched Python tests and fails on unresolved refs.

Per-shard mutation jobs have isolated 30-minute caps, use fresh archives with no persisted verdict cache, pin mutmut 3.7.0 with max-children=1 and explicit timeout inputs (timeout_constant=1.0, timeout_multiplier=15.0), and always publish structured evidence.

Promotion from advisory to ratchet requires three stable base/head pilot runs ≤24 minutes; promotion to strict requires legacy non-killed outcomes remediated or individually reviewed equivalent fingerprints.
Documentation must define phased modes, deterministic promotion evidence, false-positive policy, cadence, manifest authority, and explicitly remove legacy score tables to pass a contract test.
